Topic: Introduction to the Zambian Legal System
LearningOutcomes: Students will understand the structure of the Zambian legal system, identify the key institutions of the judiciary, and appreciate the role of law in regulating society.
LectureTopics: Overview of the Zambian legal system and its historical development
Key legal institutions: the judiciary, executive, and legislature
Sources of law: constitutions, statutes, common law, and customary law
The court hierarchy in Zambia from magistrate courts to the Supreme Court

Materials.Title: Introduction to the Zambian Legal System - Lecture Slides
Zambia Courts Act Chapter 28 - Reading Notes
Overview of the Zambian Judiciary - Reference Text

AssessmentMethods: Class participation and short reflection exercise on the role of law in society
FeedbackComments: Well-structured introduction. Good use of local examples from the Zambian judiciary.

Topic: Sources of Law: Customary Law and Statute Law
LearningOutcomes: Students will distinguish between customary law and statute law, understand how each source operates within the Zambian legal framework, and analyse conflicts between these sources.
LectureTopics: Statutory law: the legislative process and interpretation of Acts of Parliament
Customary law in Zambia: recognition, application, and limitations
Conflicts between customary law and statutory law: case studies
The role of received English law and its continued influence

Materials.Title: Sources of Law in Zambia - Lecture Slides
Customary Law and Statutory Law in Zambia - Notes
Case Study: Njobvu v The People - Reference

AssessmentMethods: Group discussion and case study analysis on customary law conflicts
FeedbackComments: Excellent contextualisation of customary law within Zambian society. Students responded well to the case studies.

LearningOutcomes: Students will understand the principles of double-entry bookkeeping, correctly record debit and credit transactions, and prepare a basic trial balance.
LectureTopics: The accounting equation: assets, liabilities, and equity
Principles of double-entry bookkeeping: debits and credits
Recording transactions in the general journal
Posting journal entries to the general ledger and preparing a trial balance

Materials.Title: Introduction to Financial Accounting - Chapter 2 Reference

AssessmentMethods: In-class bookkeeping exercise and short quiz on debit/credit rules
FeedbackComments: Clear and methodical presentation of bookkeeping fundamentals. Practice exercises are well-aligned with learning outcomes.

Topic: Overview of Healthcare Systems in Sub-Saharan Africa
LearningOutcomes: Students will compare different healthcare system models, understand the unique health challenges facing sub-Saharan Africa, and describe the structure of Zambia's national health system.
LectureTopics: Healthcare system models: Beveridge, Bismarck, and mixed systems
Overview of health challenges in sub-Saharan Africa: HIV/AIDS, malaria, and maternal health
The structure of Zambia's Ministry of Health and healthcare delivery levels
The role of NGOs and international partners in Zambian healthcare

Introduction to Global Health - Video Lecture

AssessmentMethods: Reflective journal entry on a health challenge in the student's local community
FeedbackComments: Good integration of local context with global health perspectives. Consider adding a case study from a rural district health centre.

LearningOutcomes: Students will describe the epidemiological burden of malaria in Zambia, apply key epidemiological measures to malaria data, and evaluate national malaria control strategies.
LectureTopics: The malaria parasite lifecycle and transmission dynamics in Zambia
Epidemiological measures: incidence, prevalence, and mortality rates of malaria
Zambia National Malaria Control Programme: strategies and outcomes
Vector control interventions: insecticide-treated nets and indoor residual spraying
